# W1 lane DB3: Gate 1 round 3B, database and authorisation residuals, worker provenance, decision-14 test method (`build/w1-db3`)

Scope: the round-2 DB and WORKER verifiers' residuals and new findings (`scratchpad/round2/round2-result.json`), the round-3A OPS verifier's JWKS nits (`round3a-result.json`), and the critic's MEDIUM on decision 14's test method (`critic-findings.txt`). Base `15e4e3c`. Evidence: `docs/build/evidence/W1-db3.md`. Regression tests: `backend/tests/test_security_gate1_round3b.py`, plus new tests in `test_security_gate1_worker.py` and `test_supabase_auth_jwks.py`, and the rewritten Gate 1 tests in `test_security_gate1.py` and `src/lib/__tests__/cosmologyLive.test.ts`.

| Id | Finding |
|---|---|
| R3B-API-ORIGIN | round-2 DB verifier, new MEDIUM (root cause of the R2-VIEWER-PLANT and R2-QUOTA partials): "author_user_id is null" was taken as proof that the API created a run, but `runs.author_user_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` |
| R3B-ALIAS-INDEX | round-2 DB verifier, LOW regression: `runs_tenant_client_run_id_key` (`20261102100300`) plus `ON DELETE SET NULL` made a member's account undeletable |
| R3B-SLUG-SQUAT | round-2 DB verifier, new MEDIUM: `AuthStore.issue()` adopted any existing tenant with the slug, including a user's own tenant renamed to a customer's slug |
| R3B-AGENT-DEV-GUARD | round-2 DB verifier, new LOW: `20261031200400`'s backfill re-runs on a single-version down/up and re-hands null agent rows to a user-owned `dev` |
| R3B-REDACT | round-2 DB verifier, new LOW: `redact_secrets` matched only `token` and `*_token` |
| R3B-TENANT-RESERVED | round-2 DB verifier, NIT: `AuthError` `TENANT_RESERVED` answered 500 |
| R3B-TIER-REPORT | round-2 DB verifier, R2-FORGED-REPORT residual: no report kind for non-free tiers |
| R3B-PLAN-PATH | round-2 DB verifier, R2-PLAN-PATH NIT: the plan sandbox was keyed by the (renameable) tenant slug |
| R3B-PROV-UPLOAD | round-2 WORKER verifier, c3-provenance-upload partial: an upload in flight when the attempt loses its lease still lands |
| R3B-TIMEOUT-PARSE | round-2 WORKER verifier, c3-timeout-parse NIT: `10**400` raised OverflowError; `1e-300` was accepted |
| R3B-JWKS-DEADLINE | round-3A OPS verifier, NIT: the single-flight leader fetch had no overall deadline |
| R3B-JWKS-4XX | round-3A OPS verifier, NIT: stale-if-error also served old keys after a 4xx from the JWKS endpoint |
| R3B-D14 | critic MEDIUM: Gate 1 tests that failed on `3d2355a` only by TypeError or a missing export (SF1, SF2, H2 "run reads ignore rows…", SF5 vitest case 3) |

Every finding was reproduced before it was fixed: on `15e4e3c` with the verifiers' own probes, run unchanged (`scratch-verify-DB/probes/test_author_setnull.py`, `test_alias_delete.py`, `test_slugsquat.py`; `scratch-c1/test_c1_slug.py::test_sf4_backfill_with_preexisting_user_dev_tenant_left_not_valid`; `scratch-c4-memory/test_c4_after_only.py::test_backfill_into_user_owned_dev_tenant`; `scratch-verify-WORKER/http/test_prov_inflight.py`), and on `3d2355a` for R3B-D14. None was a false positive. Migrations use `20261102120000`–`20261102120200`.

## Decisions

- **[R3B-API-ORIGIN] A service-only column, not "has a jobs row"** (`20261102120000_qcompass_run_api_origin.sql`). `public.runs.origin` is `'api'` for a run the API created and `'client'` otherwise (check constraint). The trigger `runs_origin_guard` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE) applies to every writer that `public.qcompass_privileged_writer` (round 2's `20261102100000`: the table owner or `service_role`, judged by the database role, never by a JWT claim) does not cover: on INSERT it forces `origin = 'client'`; on UPDATE a change of `origin` is `insufficient_privilege`. The SET NULL of a deleted author runs as the table owner and changes neither column, so deleting an account turns nothing into an API run.
  - Why a column: the alias index needs a predicate, and an index predicate can't hold a subquery; one marker serves the index, the reads and the quota (R20). `public.jobs` was the verifier's other option; it is what the backfill uses, once.
  - The default is `'client'`, so a privileged writer that does not say otherwise also writes a client row (fail closed). `JobQueue.enqueue_run` sets `'api'` explicitly.
  - `JobQueue._API_RUN` is now `origin = 'api'` (`get_run`, `list_runs`, the tenant-joined result query) and `plans.enforce_at_enqueue` counts `origin = 'api'` rows of the month.
  - Backfill: a run is `'api'` when it has no author, has a tenant and has a `public.jobs` row of that same tenant (`enqueue_run` writes both in one transaction; clients can't insert jobs since `20261031200100`). Runs whose author was deleted before this migration have no job and stay `'client'`; the report lists them (R3B-TIER-REPORT).
  - Down: drops the trigger and its function, restores `20261102100300`'s alias index (if author-less rows the newer rules allowed now collide, it says so with a NOTICE instead of failing), drops the check constraint, and renames the column `_deprecated_origin_20261102120000` (R13; the up renames it back).
- **[R3B-ALIAS-INDEX] Client rows never carry an alias, and the index covers API rows only** (same migration). For non-privileged writers the guard also forces `client_run_id = null` on INSERT and refuses a change on UPDATE: the alias is the API's per-tenant name for its own runs. `runs_tenant_client_run_id_key` keeps its name and becomes `(tenant_id, client_run_id) where client_run_id is not null and origin = 'api'`. Either half alone closes the regression; both together also survive a single-version rollback of `20261102100300`.
- **[R3B-SLUG-SQUAT] A key is bound to a tenant the service created, or to one named by UUID** (`AuthStore._key_tenant`, used by `issue()`). By slug: the tenant is created when missing, and an existing one is adopted only when it has no creator and no member (`auth._USER_OWNED`, the general form of round 2's `_USER_OWNED_DEV`); otherwise `AuthError("…", code="TENANT_RESERVED")` with a message telling the operator to name the tenant by UUID. By UUID: that tenant, which must exist (`UNKNOWN_TENANT` otherwise). Consequence, deliberate: once the service has added members to a tenant, a further key for it is issued by UUID (`issue(<uuid>)`), because "has members" is the only trace of an owner who cleared `created_by` before `20261102100000`.
  - Only `issue()` changes. `ensure_tenant` keeps its round-2 behaviour for the principal paths (runs, scans, memory): there the slug comes from an already-bound key or a checked membership. `add_member` and `upsert_budget` are discussed under "Routed to later tickets".
- **[R3B-TENANT-RESERVED] 409.** `HTTP_STATUS_FOR_CODE["TENANT_RESERVED"] = 409`: the request conflicts with the tenant's current owner and only a change of state (James's rename, or naming a tenant by UUID) resolves it; 403 would suggest a credential problem. `install_error_handlers` gains an `AuthError` handler that answers the mapped status with the error's code and message; an `AuthError` whose code has no status stays an opaque 500, as before.
- **[R3B-AGENT-DEV-GUARD] A trigger, whoever writes** (`20261102120200_qcompass_agent_memory_dev_guard.sql`). `qcompass_agent_memory_dev_guard` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on the six `agent_*` tables) keeps a row off a user-owned `dev` tenant (`public.qcompass_user_owned_dev`: slug `dev` with a creator or any member, the rule of `_USER_OWNED_DEV` and `20261102100100`): the row keeps its previous tenant, null for an INSERT. It applies to the owner too, because the backfill it neutralises runs as the owner. It reads and sets `tenant_id` through `to_jsonb`/`jsonb_populate_record`, so it still works while a rollback of `20261031200400` has the column renamed. Silent rather than raising: raising would make a re-run of `20261031200400` fail as a whole; null is the owner `20261102100100` chose for those rows. `20261031200400` is not edited.
- **[R3B-REDACT] Fold, then match parts.** A key is a secret when, lower-cased and without `_`, `-` and `.`, it contains `token`, `secret`, `password` or `apikey` (`_SECRET_KEY_PARTS`). That covers `approvalTokenId`, `tokenId`, `API_KEY`, `apiKey`, `client_secret`, `Password`, `refresh-token`. A non-secret key that happens to contain one of these words (e.g. `max_tokens`) is redacted too; the log loses a number, never a secret.
- **[R3B-TIER-REPORT] Two more kinds** (`20261102120100_qcompass_forged_row_report_tiers.sql`, replaces the function; down restores `20261102100200`'s body): `tenant_tier_not_free` (every tenant not on `free`: no billing integration sets tiers yet, so no paid tier can be told apart from one an owner raised before `20261102100000`) and `client_run_without_author` (client runs of a tenant whose author's account is gone: never served or counted, and no client can delete them). EXECUTE stays service-only; the migration prints a NOTICE with the count.
- **[R3B-PLAN-PATH]** `ConversationStore.save_plan` writes under `agent-sandbox/<tenant UUID>/<conversation>/plans/`. Existing plan rows keep their stored relative path; the plan payload is read from the database, so nothing is moved.
- **[R3B-PROV-UPLOAD] Per-attempt key, the row points at it.** The worker uploads `<run>/provenance-<job id>-<attempt>.json` and only the lease-checked `run_provenance` row (`artifact_path`) makes it the run's provenance. When `save_provenance` is refused, the worker deletes the object it just uploaded (`ArtifactStore.delete`, Storage's `DELETE /object/<bucket>/<name>`; a 404 counts as gone; it never raises). When the row is written and replaces an earlier attempt's object, that object is deleted too. A stale attempt's in-flight upload therefore lands on its own key, which nothing references and which it deletes, instead of on the run's object. The lease check before the put (round 2) stays.
- **[R3B-TIMEOUT-PARSE] Minimum = the wait loop's resolution.** `MIN_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = _WAIT_POLL_SECONDS = 0.1` s: `_wait_child` checks the deadline every 0.1 s, so a shorter limit can't be told apart from 0.1 s, and anything far below it only means "every job times out at once". The limit must be in [0.1, `threading.TIMEOUT_MAX`]; an int too large for a float (`10**400`) is a ValueError like every other bad value (the message says "a huge integer" instead of printing it). The env variable and the CLI go through the same check.
- **[R3B-JWKS-DEADLINE] An overall deadline for the leader.** `_JWKS_FETCH_DEADLINE_S = 5.0` s, what one httpx phase used to get, and below `_JWKS_FETCH_WAIT_S` (10 s) so waiting callers see the leader's outcome. The leader runs the fetcher in a daemon thread and gives up at the deadline (a TimeoutError, which stale-if-error treats like a network error). The default fetcher streams the body and stops reading once the deadline has passed, so the abandoned thread ends too; it also refuses bodies over 1 MiB.
- **[R3B-JWKS-4XX] Stale-if-error for network errors, timeouts and 5xx only.** An `httpx.HTTPStatusError` with a 4xx status (401, 403, 404: the project or its keys are gone) drops the cached set for the URL at once and is a 503; the retry interval still applies. This also covers a 4xx on a forced (unknown-kid) refetch, which drops a set that was still within its TTL. 408 and 429 are 4xx and are treated the same way, as the instruction says ("only on network errors/5xx"); with one fetch per URL per TTL and the 30 s back-off, the API itself cannot provoke a 429.
- **[R3B-D14] Behaviour first, then the post-fix API.** Each rewritten Gate 1 test starts with steps and checks that use only HTTP, SQL or calls that exist on `3d2355a`, so it fails there on the bug, and then keeps every assertion it had (including the ones that use the post-fix signatures). Details under "Corrected tests".

## Corrected tests (old → new, proof)

"Before" for the round-3B items is `15e4e3c`; for R3B-D14 it is `3d2355a`. Logs are listed in the evidence file.

- **[R3B-D14] `backend/tests/test_security_gate1.py::test_h2_run_reads_ignore_rows_written_under_another_tenant`** (rewritten, tightened).
  - Old: seeded globex's run, `q.emit(None, run, acme, "status", {"completed", forged})`, `q.save_result(...)`, then `q.events(run, tenant_uuid=victim)`, `q.result(..., tenant_uuid=...)`, `q.result_text(..., tenant_uuid=...)`. On `3d2355a`: `TypeError: JobQueue.events() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tenant_uuid'`.
  - New: the same forged event, plus a provenance row filed under acme (`q.save_provenance(run, acme, …)`, which `3d2355a` has), and globex's own terminal event; then globex's `GET …/runs/run_mixed` must not show "forged" and its SSE stream (bounded) must not replay it and must end. Then every old assertion, plus `q.provenance(run, tenant_uuid=victim) is None`. On `3d2355a`: `AssertionError: the run shows provenance filed under another tenant`. On `15e4e3c` and this branch: pass.
- **[R3B-D14] `…::test_sf1_dead_letter_fails_the_run_and_writes_a_terminal_event`** (rewritten, tightened).
  - Old: set the run running with the lease (`set_run_status(…, job_id=, worker_id=, attempt=)`), reaped, then read events with `tenant_uuid=`. On `3d2355a`: `TypeError: JobQueue.set_run_status() got an unexpected keyword argument 'job_id'`.
  - New: the dying worker sets the run running with the lease-free call every tree has; after the reap, the run must be failed and `q.events(run)` must end with the failed status event; then the tenant-filtered events give the same last event; added: the dead attempt's lease-carrying write (`set_run_status(…, "completed", job_id=…, attempt=…)`) is refused. The stream check is unchanged. On `3d2355a`: `AssertionError: the dead-lettered job left its run running` (`'running' == 'failed'`). On `15e4e3c` and this branch: pass. The lease on the "running" write was incidental to SF1; lease-carrying writes are covered by the SF2 tests and the new last assertion.
- **[R3B-D14] `…::test_sf2_a_stale_worker_cannot_touch_a_reclaimed_job`** (tightened).
  - Old: every step after the reclaim used the post-fix signatures (`complete(…, worker_id=, attempt=)`, lease kwargs). On `3d2355a`: `TypeError` on the first `set_run_status(…, job_id=…)`.
  - New: right after B claims the reclaimed job, worker A calls main's completion RPC through SQL as the service role, `public.complete_job(job, result, error)` (every tree has it; on the fixed tree it raises), and B's job must still be running. Then every old step and assertion, unchanged. On `3d2355a`: `AssertionError: a stale worker completed the job another worker holds` (`'succeeded' == 'running'`). On `15e4e3c` and this branch: pass.
- **[R3B-D14] `src/lib/__tests__/cosmologyLive.test.ts` case 3, "reads agent (ucgle_f1.run) payloads, which are the RunResult itself, on the same route"** (rewritten, tightened).
  - Old: called `cosmologyRunResult(...)` directly. On `3d2355a`: `cosmologyRunResult is not a function` (the export did not exist).
  - New: a fetch mock that serves the agent run on the platform route (payload = the RunResult) and also on the legacy `/api/runs/run_a` route, as the backend does; `getRun("run_a")` (present on `3d2355a`) must return it and must have fetched only the platform route; then the old direct call. On `3d2355a`: `expected [ 'http://api.test/api/runs/run_a' ] to deeply equal [ …/api/qcompass/domains/cosmology.ucglef1/runs/run_a ]`, i.e. `getRun` read the legacy route, the route split SF5 removed. For an agent run that legacy route still answered on `3d2355a`, so this case is not counted as SF5's regression test; case 1 is (on `3d2355a` it fails with `ServiceError` NOT_FOUND from `GET /api/runs/qc_c1`, without waiting for the run). Case 2 passes on both trees and is a guard.
- **[R3B-API-ORIGIN] `backend/tests/test_plan_limits.py::test_runs_per_month_at_and_over_the_boundary`** (setup only).
  - Old: the 30 last-month and 24 this-month rows standing for API runs were inserted with no author, which round 2 took as "API-created".
  - New: the same rows are inserted with `origin = 'api'`, as `enqueue_run` writes them. Assertions unchanged (25th run allowed, 26th is `PLAN_RUNS_PER_MONTH_EXCEEDED` with limit 25, used 25). Proof: the old version on this branch fails with `DID NOT RAISE PlanLimitExceeded`, because author-less rows are no longer API runs (exactly the R3B-API-ORIGIN fix); the new version can't run on `15e4e3c` (no `origin` column).
- **[R3B-SLUG-SQUAT] `backend/tests/test_security_gate1_round2.py::test_r2_owner_cannot_raise_their_own_plan`** (setup only).
  - Old: `get_auth_store().issue(slug, …)` with the slug of alice's personal tenant.

Proof: the old version on this branch fails at `issue()` with `AuthError TENANT_RESERVED` (a user's tenant is never adopted by slug: the fix); the new version passes on `15e4e3c` too.
- **[R3B-TIER-REPORT] `…::test_r2_forged_row_report_lists_and_keeps_forged_rows`** (expected set extended).
  - Old: the report equals exactly the three forged rows.
  - New: the three forged rows plus `("tenant_tier_not_free", acme)` and `("tenant_tier_not_free", globex)`, the fixture's two enterprise tenants. Proof: the fixture sets both tiers to `enterprise`; the new kind lists every non-free tier by design. On `15e4e3c` the new version fails (the tier rows are missing: the residual itself).
- **[R3B-PLAN-PATH] `…::test_r2_plans_stay_in_the_tenant_sandbox_and_store_a_relative_path`** (expected path).
  - Old: `plan.path == f"agent-sandbox/{tenant}/c_shared/plans/{plan.planId}.json"` with the slug.
  - New: the same with the tenant's UUID. The other assertions (unsafe ids refused, nothing escaped, relative path, file content) unchanged. Proof: the slug key is the finding; on `15e4e3c` the new version fails on the path, the old version fails on this branch on the path.
- **[R3B-PROV-UPLOAD] `backend/tests/test_worker_queue.py::test_provenance_is_a_row_and_a_run_artifacts_object`** (pinned path).
  - Old: `artifact_path == f"run-artifacts/{run_id}/provenance.json"`, and the single request's path is that object.
  - New: `artifact_path == f"run-artifacts/{run_id}/provenance-{job_id}-{attempt}.json"` (job id and attempt read from `public.jobs`), the single request is a POST to that path. Everything else unchanged (one upload, status `stored`, hash in the object and the API response). Proof: the fixed name is the finding (a stale attempt's upload overwrote the reclaiming attempt's object); old version on this branch and new version on `15e4e3c` each fail on the path only.

No test was removed or skipped.

## Removals with replacement

- **[R3B-API-ORIGIN]** "No author means the API created the run" (`JobQueue._API_RUN = "author_user_id is null"`, the result query, `plans.enforce_at_enqueue`, the alias index predicate) → `runs.origin = 'api'`, a service-only column.
- **[R3B-ALIAS-INDEX]** Clients writing `runs.client_run_id` → forced null for non-privileged writers on insert, refused on update.
- **[R3B-SLUG-SQUAT]** `AuthStore.issue()` adopting any tenant with the slug (`ensure_tenant`) → `_key_tenant`: by slug only a tenant with no creator and no member, else by UUID.
- **[R3B-PLAN-PATH]** `agent-sandbox/<tenant slug>/…` → `agent-sandbox/<tenant UUID>/…`.
- **[R3B-PROV-UPLOAD]** One fixed object per run, `<run>/provenance.json` → one object per attempt, referenced by the row; unreferenced ones deleted.
- **[R3B-JWKS-4XX]** Stale-if-error on any fetch failure → on network errors, timeouts and 5xx only.
- **[R3B-TIMEOUT-PARSE]** Job time limits in (0, `TIMEOUT_MAX`] → in [0.1, `TIMEOUT_MAX`] s.

## Routed to later tickets

- **[R3B-SLUG-SQUAT] `add_member` and `upsert_budget` still create-or-adopt by slug** (`ensure_tenant`). They are operator-only, not reachable over HTTP, and an operator provisions a customer with `issue()` first, which now refuses a squatted slug. The "no member" rule can't apply to `add_member`, whose purpose is to add members to service tenants, and `created_by is null` alone misses an owner who cleared it before `20261102100000`. Closing it needs a positive "service-managed" marker on `public.tenants`, like `runs.origin`; routed to P7-07, whose invite flow is the first customer-provisioning path.
- **[R3B-API-ORIGIN] `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts`** does not list `runs.origin` (nor round 2's `client_run_id`). It is generated from the live Supabase project, which has none of these migrations (`BLOCKED-ON-JAMES:DATABASE_URL`); regenerate it after the first deploy. No frontend code reads either column.
- **[R3B-PROV-UPLOAD]** An attempt whose own `DELETE` fails (Storage down) leaves an unreferenced object under the run's prefix; it is logged, and no row references it. A sweep of `run-artifacts` objects that no `run_provenance.artifact_path` names is routed to P6-02's runbooks.

## BLOCKED-ON-JAMES

- **[all]** `BLOCKED-ON-JAMES:DATABASE_URL`: none of the three migrations has been applied to a real project. Each was applied, rolled back and re-applied on the local Postgres 16 harness (`test_r3b_migrations_are_reversible`).
- **[R3B-TIER-REPORT][R3B-API-ORIGIN]** After the first deploy, James reviews `select * from public.qcompass_forged_row_report() where kind in ('tenant_tier_not_free', 'client_run_without_author')` (service role); the migration NOTICE gives the count. Nothing is changed or deleted automatically. No new secret name is introduced.
